author: NASASpaceflight
description:
SpaceX is proposing up to 456 Starship launches a year from Starbase, while Flight 15 is targeting no earlier than November 8 with plans to catch both Starship and Super Heavy. Meanwhile, Ship 40 has returned home after 75 days at sea following Flight 13.

In this week’s Starship Update, we cover Ship 42’s engine reinstallation and cryogenic testing, Booster 23’s move to Massey’s, and the next vehicles taking shape inside Starfactory.

We also break down the proposed two-phase expansion of Starbase operations, check progress at Florida’s LC-39A, follow Raptor testing at McGregor, and take a closer look at Ship 40’s journey back to Starbase.

The proposed launch increases remain subject to environmental review and FAA approval. Flight 15’s target date and recovery plans are also subject to change.

Will Flight 15 achieve the first catch of both vehicles? And what should SpaceX do with Ship 40 now that it’s home? Share your thoughts in the comments.
